doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Why the queen rides before the king
summary: Edna explains why the queen leads the king in a ladies' organization, from the first mademoiselles.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What do you want to put the.
Oh, the king before the queen. Yeah.
Now, have you ever heard of this? The king before.
Oh, he never changes. The king before the queen.

So I said, why? Oh, it is always a rule that the king always precedes the queen. I said, but this is a ladies organization. Well, no matter. I said, well, yes, it does matter in this organization. Because on the beginning, we didn't have a queen. We called, my little granddaughter was the first mademoiselle fiesta. We called them mademoiselle fiesta. You see? We didn't have no queenship or anything. We called them mademoiselle. And I said, she was the first. And she was the first one to ride ahead of all the rest. Mademoiselle. Now, we had those for three or four years. Yeah, three years. Three or four years we had these mademoiselle fiestas. And Eliska Pelleborn, one of my board members, her little granddaughter, was the first queen. So as we grow older, we began to talk. We said, well, let's make a queen instead of...

A queen, but we didn't have a king. We still didn't have a king. And so I said, well, all right. We have to go on. You know, go on. We just can't stay the same way if it's all right. So then we had this first queen. And so on. I think this is the third or fourth year we had a queen. And then the king, about the fifth year we had a queen. And the king about the third year.
Third year you had the king.

The king. So now when we had the king, we already had the queen. So we weren't going to put the queen behind the king. And it's a ladies organization. And we had her first. Why put the man first and we've already had the... You understand what I mean? I thought there was something to it that we should honor and keep it. And so I told him that. Oh, it doesn't matter. It doesn't matter. A king is always ahead of the queen. I said, now listen, Sergeant Norbert. If that's going to do you any good to change the route of the parade. I said, take it over because I've been ill now. And I don't want to get sick now. Take it over. Oh, no, Ms. Senegal, I don't want to take it over. I said, take it over. Take it over. And I just hung up on him. He went and she... Ms. Bozang called, Ms. Senegal, you're not getting sick now. I said, listen, I can't be bothered anymore. I said, you see, I've been well and it can't go the way it is. There's no need to have been all night. You know, I mean, just take it over and do it. What did they do? All policemen at the office sure left at him. He went on back to work. And so Ms. Bozang called him back and said, now listen, Sergeant Norbert, you better, if you don't want Ms. Senegal to get sick, you better come on back here and change this route. Because I can't even talk to her. She's in the bed with a pillow on her head and she gave up the fiesta and everything. And anytime she gives up the fiesta, that's the end. So he came on back, he told the officers, please do his work for him by the time he go back there with those ladders. They kid him. They said that man couldn't do his work. Who was the ladders? The ladders had it. And when he went back there, he said the ladders, the ladders, uh, he had to submit to the ladders. So when he came back there, he said, Ms. Senegal, what's the matter? I don't want to make you sick. I said, no. He said, I'll do just exactly the way you sit. Does that suit you? I say, just have it the way I want it or else. So he said, yes, madam, yes, madam, it'll be the way you want it. I didn't care for you the boss. I said, no, I don't want to be the boss of anybody or anything. But just, I think that's the right way. And that's the way I want it. Yes, ma'am. And here, what was the cause on a parade day?
